title: Quasi-compactness of a site object and its sheafified representable
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $U\in\mathcal C$, and put $H_U=h_U^\#$, where $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The following conditions are equivalent. (i) For every covering family $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ there is a covering family $(V_j\to U)_{j\in J}$ refining it, with a function $\alpha:J\to I$ of finite image and maps $V_j\to U_{\alpha(j)}$ over $U$. (ii) $H_U$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos], that is, every epimorphism $\coprod_{i\in I}F_i\to H_U$ of sheaves of sets restricts to an epimorphism $\coprod_{i\in I_0}F_i\to H_U$ for some finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$.

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact; condition (i) is Definition 090H, definition-quasi-compact.

proof.text: Assume (i) and let $p:\coprod_{i\in I}F_i\to H_U$ be epi. By [lem-trf-site-epimorphic-family-cover-lifts], choose a covering $(u_a:U_a\to U)_a$, labels $\iota(a)\in I$, and sections $s_a\in F_{\iota(a)}(U_a)$ mapping to $\eta_U(u_a)$. Apply (i) to this covering, obtaining a covering $(v_c:V_c\to U)_c$ refining it via $\alpha:C\to A$ with finite image. Restrict $s_{\alpha(c)}$ to $V_c$. Naturality gives a lift of $\eta_U(v_c)$ in the summand indexed by $\iota(\alpha(c))$. The set $I_0=\iota(\operatorname{im}\alpha)$ is finite. Apply the converse of the same cited criterion to $(F_i\to H_U)_{i\in I_0}$ and this covering: its coproduct map is epi. This proves (ii).

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact, forward implication: the finite image of the refinement index map.

proof.text: Assume (ii) and take a covering $(a_i:U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$. In [lem-trf-site-epimorphic-family-cover-lifts], use the sheaves $F_i=H_{U_i}$, their induced maps to $H_U$, this covering, and the sections $\eta_{U_i}(\operatorname{id}_{U_i})$. Naturality of sheafification identifies their images with $\eta_U(a_i)$, so the coproduct map $\coprod_iH_{U_i}\to H_U$ is epi. Condition (ii) gives a finite $I_0\subseteq I$ such that $\coprod_{i\in I_0}H_{U_i}\to H_U$ is still epi.

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact, reverse implication through selection of a finite epimorphic subfamily.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-site-sheafified-arrows-cover-refinement] to the arrow family $(a_i:U_i\to U)_{i\in I_0}$ and its epimorphic sheaf coproduct from step 2. It gives a covering $(V_b\to U)_b$ with arrows $V_b\to U_{\alpha(b)}$ over $U$, where $\alpha:B\to I_0$. Compose $\alpha$ with the inclusion $I_0\hookrightarrow I$. Its image is contained in the finite set $I_0$, so this is exactly the covering refinement required in (i).

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact, reverse implication: the genuine covering refinement has indices in the selected finite subset.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact proof; Definition 090H for the site condition

lean.statement: theorem site_quasiCompact_iff_sheafifiedYoneda_quasiCompact {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : Precoverage C) (_hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (U : C) : (∀ (I : Type (max u v)) (U_i : I → C) (a : ∀ i, U_i i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows U_i a ∈ J U → ∃ (K : Type (max u v)) (V : K → C) (b : ∀ k, V k ⟶ U) (α : K → I) (c : ∀ k, V k ⟶ U_i (α k)), Set.Finite (Set.range α) ∧ (∀ k, c k ≫ a (α k) = b k) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows V b ∈ J U) ↔ IsQuasiCompactObject.{max u v} ((presheafToSheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u v))).obj (uliftYoneda.{u}.obj U))
